meta.definition: Editorial comparison of what external AI can read, write and how easily it connects. Same combined lens across categories; not a vendor-quality score.

statusDefinition.Production: Dependable enough for a controlled recurring workflow today.
statusDefinition.Test: Worth piloting, but access, maturity or control needs a bounded test.
statusDefinition.Research: Useful specialist capability, not a daily operating interface.

positives: Read campaign structure, metrics and GAQL reports.
Create assets and manage labels, not campaigns or budgets.
negatives: Campaign changes still require another route; video upload is local only.

positives: Official hosted campaign reads, creation, editing and activation.
OAuth access without a mandatory developer app.
negatives: General rollout is unconfirmed. Some creative formats have limited availability; campaign deletion is not documented.

positives: Read campaign information, reports and audience context.
Create campaigns and change budgets, bids and targeting.
negatives: Exact deletion and launch tools remain unverified.

positives: Read campaigns, keywords, assets, reports and change history.
Register an Entra app, configure OAuth and connect the hosted MCP.
negatives: Hosted does not mean one-click: ChatGPT and Claude need an Entra app registration.

positives: Read performance, account and billing information.
Create, update and delete supported campaigns.
negatives: Open beta with partner/API access; not every ad product is covered.

positives: Read authorised campaign setup and performance.
An administrator approves the agent; each member grants access.
negatives: Self-service access still requires organisation approval and member consent.

positives: Read campaign configuration and performance through approved APIs.
Create and manage campaigns through custom API code.
negatives: No ready official agent connector verified; use a supported API version.

positives: Read campaigns, ad groups and performance.
Create and manage campaigns, ad groups and ads via API.
negatives: Custom integration required. The announced official MCP is not yet verified as launched.

positives: Read campaign information and reports through API v3.
Create campaigns and update budgets, schedules and delivery status.
negatives: Custom AI integration required. Activation does not bypass ad approval or billing checks.

positives: Read campaign structure, analytics, audiences and creative assets.
Build and edit campaigns, then activate them explicitly.
negatives: Developer-app OAuth setup remains; selected deletes exclude campaign deletion.

positives: Read trafficking resources; use a separate route for performance reports.
Manage supported resources, including responsive YouTube ads in v5 beta.
negatives: Public beta. YouTube line-item, ad-group and targeting setup still requires the interface or SDF upload.

positives: Read campaign resources and reports via API v5.
Create campaigns and reports; update supported campaign fields.
negatives: A custom trafficking integration is needed; archive is not deletion.

positives: Query campaign-to-keyword resources and performance reports.
Build an authenticated API integration and maintain it.
negatives: Custom setup still stops at diagnosis; campaign changes happen elsewhere.

positives: Read campaign configuration, reports and performance.
Create, edit and delete campaign resources; enable eligible ads.
negatives: Custom AI integration required. Enabled status does not guarantee serving.

positives: Vendor-hosted access to campaign data and reports.
negatives: Closed beta. The capability table marks reads available but still dates configuration writes to H2 2026.

positives: Read properties, dimensions, key events and analytics reports.
Create annotations, custom dimensions and key events with writes enabled.
negatives: Self-managed setup. Writes only create annotations, custom dimensions and key events.

positives: Read accounts, containers, workspaces, tags and versions.
Change configuration, create previews and publish container versions.
negatives: Third-party connection, not Google-operated. Publishing still needs tracking and consent checks.

positives: Query analytics and inspect charts, cohorts, experiments and taxonomy.
Create and edit analytical content and tracking definitions; sync cohorts to destinations.
negatives: Guides/surveys stop at drafts; definition changes do not ingest production events.

positives: Read events, funnels, retention, saved reports and data-quality issues.
Manage dashboards and cohorts; update definitions and resolve data issues.
negatives: Experiment and flag tools are beta; audience targeting needs the UI. EU and India use custom connectors.

positives: Read connected marketing accounts, fields and cross-channel performance.
Create paused campaigns and edit supported budgets, ads and settings.
negatives: Third-party access to ad platforms. Writes need owner opt-in; supported actions vary by platform.

positives: Retrieve SERP, keyword, backlink and competitor research data.
Submit billable research tasks; no campaign or website mutations.
negatives: Research execution is not campaign control; API endpoint costs and allowances apply.

positives: Read connector configuration, sync status, logs and supported external records.
Manage connectors and pipelines; start or cancel syncs.
negatives: Direct record access is read-only. Deletes require a marked resource name; connectors and credentials need prior setup.

positives: Query the prepared warehouse context layer with read-only SQL.
Submit answer feedback only; no operational data changes.
negatives: Public Preview. An administrator must build the context layer and grant access; business data remains read-only.

positives: Query configured databases and inspect their schemas.
Execute only the database operations exposed by your toolset.
negatives: Requires local or hosted server setup and database credentials. Operations and read-only controls vary by database and toolset.

positives: Query governed data through configured SQL and Cortex tools.
Optional SQL and custom tools can change data when explicitly enabled.
negatives: An administrator must expose tools and grant access. SQL is read-only by default; writes need explicit configuration.

positives: Inspect prepared data, model results and convergence diagnostics.
Run modelling scripts and produce saved models and budget scenarios.
negatives: Runs in a coding environment, not a hosted chat app. Data mappings, priors and model execution need human review.

positives: Read prepared historical data and inspect model outputs through code.
Fit models and generate diagnostics and allocation scenarios.
negatives: Requires modelling code and prepared data. Python is beta; no ready official chat connector was verified.

positives: Read prepared data and fitted Bayesian models through Python.
Create models, diagnostics, forecasts and allocation scenarios.
negatives: Requires Python, prepared data and modelling expertise. No ready chat connector was verified for this library.

positives: Read and search records in connected apps.
Run supported app actions; workflow creation is separate early access.
negatives: Coverage depends on each app; Next Gen Zaps deployment is not available to every account.

positives: Search and retrieve records from connected apps.
Create and update app records through hosted actions.
negatives: Each app has its own tools; app actions do not establish Pipedream workflow authoring.

positives: Read exposed workflows, executions and supported data tables.
Create, edit, test, publish and unpublish workflows.
negatives: Enable MCP per instance and workflow. Version gates and protected-instance restrictions apply.

positives: Read design structure, components, variables and file context.
Create and edit native canvas objects in supported clients.
negatives: Canvas writing is beta; library publishing stays manual and visual review remains necessary.

positives: Read designs, pages, content, folders and permitted brand templates.
Create and edit designs, transform images and export assets.
negatives: Plan and admin limits apply. Deletion and publishing are unverified; exporting a design does not publish it.

positives: Read reports, components, date ranges and workspace projects.
Create or update segments, calculated metrics and projects.
negatives: No delete tool is listed; component writes do not configure collection tags.

positives: Read data views, components, audiences, projects and reports.
Create or update analytical components, projects and audiences.
negatives: No general deletion or connection administration; audience creation does not prove downstream activation.

positives: Read analytics, SQL/schema, insights, errors and pipeline diagnostics.
Manage dashboards, insights, flags, experiments and supported pipelines.
negatives: Events must already be collected; some AI tools can incur additional usage costs.

positives: Read aggregate performance, creative, SKAN and configuration data.
Create OneLink short links under existing templates, with confirmation.
negatives: Beta. Ten new OneLink links per account per day; broader account editing is not documented.

positives: Read aggregate Adjust performance data.
No Adjust account mutations are documented for this MCP.
negatives: Early Access requires enablement; no user-level or event-level data.

positives: Read workspace sources, destinations, warehouses and tracking plans through API.
Manage supported workspace resources through a custom API integration.
negatives: Requires a custom API integration. The Twilio MCP retrieves documentation only, not account data.

positives: Discover actions/templates, check run status and retrieve outputs.
Compose creative workflows, transform media and publish reusable workflows.
negatives: Organisation credentials are required; output links expire and publishing does not distribute ads.

positives: Retrieve generated outputs; general library search is unverified.
Generate images/videos and perform supported reference-based transformations.
negatives: Every generation and retry uses credits. Library management, deletion and ad or social publishing are unverified.

positives: Retrieve keyword, backlink, domain and SEO research reports.
Create, organise and delete projects through explicitly MCP-enabled endpoints.
negatives: Project management does not edit a website. Some keyword mutations remain API-only; dataset and API-unit limits apply.

positives: Read SEO, Trends and supported Projects reports.
Read-only; project creation and settings changes are excluded.
negatives: MCP does not inherit wider REST API mutations; API units and subscribed datasets apply.

positives: Read website/app, audience, traffic, search and commerce intelligence.
No account, campaign or content writes established.
negatives: The connector exposes subscribed datasets only and consumes data credits.

positives: Read source, destination, transformation and event context.
Destination configuration is documented; exact create, delete and publish tools remain unverified.
negatives: The vendor warns of active development and variable stability. Exact write tools and release maturity are not fully documented.

positives: Run SQL against governed tables and inspect database schemas.
Execute SQL writes within warehouse permissions; administrators can disable writes.
negatives: SQL MCP is Beta and needs admin enablement. Genie One is a separate generally available route; its status does not cover SQL writes.

positives: Read metrics, model context, lineage, freshness, jobs and SQL results.
Trigger, retry or cancel jobs; execute SQL with development credentials.
negatives: OAuth is public beta. SQL uses personal development credentials; local project commands require the separate self-hosted server.

positives: Read authorised scenarios, connections, teams and organisation context.
Modify supported automation assets and run authorised scenarios.
negatives: Management requires a paid plan and scopes. Creation, deletion and activation tools are unverified.

positives: Read permitted projects, folders, connections, jobs and workspace assets.
Manage role-enabled workspace resources and exposed business tools.
negatives: API-client roles and tokens are required. Deletion and recipe deployment remain unverified; China is excluded.

positives: Read agents, sessions, artifacts, tools, flows and permitted knowledge sources.
Create and edit agents/skills, run them and manage supported triggers.
negatives: Personal/team scopes differ; complete visual-flow authoring is not established.
